candidates.title: The Adoration of the Magi
candidates.comments: KMSKA museum oil 1624–25; large expressive altar panel, photo terms need exact check
candidates.depicts: The Magi kneel before the Christ Child in a monumental Baroque setting.

candidates.title: The Adoration of the Magi
candidates.comments: Boijmans museum oil c1655, richly Baroque, exact museum image reuse not certified
candidates.depicts: Wise men offer gifts to the Child in a richly populated Flemish interior.

candidates.title: The Adoration of the Magi
candidates.comments: Japanese NMWA museum oil c1687–89, wide Baroque painting; photograph terms unverified
candidates.depicts: The visiting kings and their retinue gather at the Nativity.

liturgical_1962.reading_summary: The nations and kings are drawn to Jerusalem's light; the Magi follow the star, adore the Child and offer gold, frankincense and myrrh.
liturgical_1962.theme: Manifestation of Christ to the Gentiles

candidates.title: The Lamentation over the Dead Christ
candidates.comments: KMSKA c1640, Christ at rock-hewn tomb and Virgin grief; strong Baroque horizontal canvas; photograph rights source-specific
candidates.depicts: The Virgin and disciples mourn the dead Christ at the tomb.

candidates.title: The Lamentation over the Dead Christ
candidates.comments: KMSKA 1614 oil on panel, 55×73cm, dramatically lit grief; exact photo licence not presumed
candidates.depicts: The dead Christ is mourned by those closest to Him.

liturgical_1962.reading_summary: Creation and deliverance prepare for baptism and the Resurrection; the women find the empty tomb and hear the angel's proclamation that Christ is risen.
liturgical_1962.theme: From the darkness of the tomb to the victory of the Resurrection

candidates.artist: Anonymous Venetian (possibly Lambert Sustris), formerly attributed to Tintoretto
candidates.title: Christ at the Sea of Galilee
candidates.comments: NGA official open image; scholarly record confirms *post-Resurrection John 21*, seven apostles and dawn; avoid asserting Tintoretto authorship
candidates.depicts: At dawn the risen Christ directs the seven disciples' nets from the shore; Peter prepares to leap into the water.

candidates.title: The Miraculous Draught of Fishes
candidates.comments: 1444 Geneva altarpiece; contains John 21 catch with Matthew 14 Peter-on-water motif; photographic rights remain uncertain

previous_candidate.title: Christ at the Sea of Galilee
previous_candidate.rejection_reason: NGA object is Peter rescued from water (Matthew 14), not the Resurrection fishing scene (John 21); subject mismatch

candidates.depicts: Christ stands near Lake Geneva imagined as Galilee while the Apostles make the miraculous catch; image combines the catch with Peter on the water.

liturgical_1962.reading_summary: Peter preaches Christ's Resurrection; at dawn the risen Lord appears to seven disciples by Lake Tiberias, tells them to cast the net and offers them bread and fish.
liturgical_1962.theme: Risen Christ on the shore; the miraculous catch of 153 fish

candidates.title: Noli me Tangere
candidates.comments: National Gallery, London c1514; full oil, Gospel exact; current NG reproduction terms unsuitable for unrestricted derivatives
candidates.depicts: Risen Christ meets Mary Magdalene in the garden, who turns to Him in recognition.

candidates.title: Noli me tangere
candidates.comments: Alte Pinakothek Munich inv494; late 16th-century oil; independent image reuse verification pending
candidates.depicts: Christ appears to Mary Magdalene after His Resurrection.

liturgical_1962.reading_summary: Philip baptizes the Ethiopian official; Mary Magdalene recognizes the risen Jesus when He calls her by name, and He tells her not to cling to Him.

candidates.artist: Johannes Wierix, after Gerard van Groeningen
candidates.title: The Paralytic Lowered through the Roof
candidates.comments: Rijksmuseum public-domain engraving, full composition precisely illustrates Luke 5; monochrome, not oil
candidates.depicts: The friends of a paralyzed man lower him through the roof before Jesus, who forgives and heals him.

candidates.title: The Palsied Man Let Down through the Roof
candidates.comments: Brooklyn Museum watercolor, physically exact John/Luke gospel scene; photo-use to confirm
candidates.depicts: Tissot renders the crowded house and disabled man descending through the roof.

liturgical_1962.reading_summary: God promises abundance and His abiding presence; Jesus forgives and heals the paralytic lowered through the roof.
liturgical_1962.theme: Healing of body and soul in the Pentecost octave

candidates.title: Christ as Man of Sorrows at the Foot of the Cross
candidates.comments: NGA public-domain engraving; Christ with visible chalice and Eucharistic bread; new more precise subject but not an oil painting
candidates.depicts: Christ as the Man of Sorrows and signs of the Eucharist: a symbolic depiction of Blood and redemption, not the physical lance wound.

candidates.artist: Jacques de Gheyn II, after Karel van Mander I
candidates.title: Christ in the Winepress
candidates.comments: Met public-domain engraving c1596–98; Precious Blood symbolic winepress imagery, not an oil painting
candidates.depicts: Christ is pressed like grapes in a mystical winepress, an allegory of His Blood poured out for salvation.

liturgical_1962.reading_summary: Christ enters the sanctuary as High Priest through His own Blood; at the Crucifixion His side is pierced and blood and water flow out.

candidates.title: Archangel Michael Defeating Satan
candidates.comments: Reuse existing Saint Michael module and user-selected Guardian Angel module painting; original-image photographic gate already documented
candidates.depicts: Armoured Michael triumphs over Satan. This is traditional Michael iconography, not the Gospel scene of children and guardian angels.

candidates.title: Saint Michael the Archangel
candidates.comments: Met official Open Access/CC0, c1640s; distinct Spanish Baroque archangel portrait
candidates.depicts: Michael stands armed above evil in a bright Baroque heavenly vision; it illustrates his victory, not the exact Matthew reading.

liturgical_1962.reading_summary: God's revelation is communicated through an angel; Christ speaks of little children, humility and their angels who behold the Father's face.
liturgical_1962.theme: Heavenly angels as servants of God and protectors of the faithful

candidates.title: The Immaculate Conception
candidates.comments: Cleveland c1680 full painting official OA; crescent moon, angels, warm-cloud Baroque
candidates.depicts: The Virgin is suspended above the crescent moon among angels, immaculate and triumphant; iconography of the doctrine.

candidates.title: The Immaculate Conception
candidates.comments: Metropolitan Museum original accession 59.32, Guido Reni The Immaculate Conception (1627), official Open Access photo, lighter than Murillo but major altarpiece
candidates.depicts: Reni depicts Mary surrounded by heavenly light as the Immaculate Virgin.

liturgical_1962.reading_summary: The liturgy applies Wisdom's ancient words to Mary's privileges; Gabriel greets her as full of grace. The feast celebrates Mary's preservation from original sin.
liturgical_1962.theme: Immaculate Conception, not the conception of Christ at the Annunciation

candidates.title: The Annunciation to the Shepherds
candidates.comments: NGA OA c1555–60, exact annunciation to shepherds as thematic anticipation (event itself belongs to Christmas night, not vigil Gospel)
candidates.depicts: An angel announces the birth of Christ to shepherds at night; event occurs AFTER the birth in Luke 2, not in this day's Matthew Gospel.

candidates.title: Adoration of the Shepherds
candidates.comments: Cleveland OA c1510 dark Nativity with Joseph's candle; anticipatory rather than vigil Gospel; user dislikes old-Joseph depictions, inspect
candidates.depicts: Shepherds adore the newborn Child; Christmas-night subject, not the Vigil's Joseph dream.

candidates.title: Joseph's Dream
candidates.comments: c.1790 oil painting; angel addresses young/mature sleeping Joseph; Matthew 1:18–25 direct Gospel, photo source Commons faithful-image claim needs exact check
candidates.depicts: Joseph sleeps while an angel tells him to receive Mary and accept the coming Child; corresponds directly to the Vigil Gospel.

liturgical_1962.reading_summary: Christ is the promised descendant of David; an angel tells Joseph to receive Mary, for her child is conceived of the Holy Ghost, and to name Him Jesus.
liturgical_1962.theme: Joseph's obedience and expectancy before the Nativity

candidates.title: Adoration of the Shepherds
candidates.comments: Cleveland OA, Neapolitan dark interior around radiant Child and Gloria angels
candidates.depicts: The shepherds kneel by the manger in a dark Neapolitan setting lit by the newborn Christ; especially suited to the Midnight and Dawn Gospels.

candidates.title: Adoration of the Shepherds
candidates.comments: Cleveland OA c1670, vertical dark-cloud baroque; includes Joseph, test age depiction
candidates.depicts: The Holy Family, shepherds and Child in a luminous vertical Nativity; chiefly Luke 2, and thematically the Incarnation of John's prologue.

liturgical_1962.reading_summary: Three Christmas Masses: at Midnight the birth and angelic announcement; at Dawn the shepherds visit the Child; by Day the eternal Word made flesh.
liturgical_1962.theme: One shared Christmas hero must work across the three Masses
